key_insight: HVOF-sprayed Ni-20Cr+40TiC coating delivered the best oxidation protection on SA516 boiler steel, cutting maximum weight gain by 95.71% versus bare steel at 900°C.
engineering_relevance: For high-temperature boiler and thermal-service components, Ni-Cr ceramic composite coatings can greatly improve oxidation resistance by forming dense protective oxides and limiting spallation.
method: Compared Ni-20Cr, Ni-20Cr+40TiC, and Ni-20Cr+40TiN coatings on SA516 steel.
Applied both HVOF and plasma spray deposition routes.
Evaluated cyclic oxidation for 50 cycles at 900°C using XRD, SEM/EDS, and X-ray mapping.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports cyclic air oxidation data showing severe spalling in uncoated steel, while the HVOF Ni-20Cr+40TiC coating achieved the lowest weight gain and the most protective oxide scale.
watch_item: Results are from laboratory cyclic oxidation only, so long-term service performance under real boiler thermal gradients, erosion, and steam chemistry still needs validation.
paper_title: Microstructure and High-Temperature Oxidation Behaviour of HVOF and Plasma Sprayed Ni–Cr-Based Ceramic Coatings on SA516 Boiler Steel
